prompt: On a reviewer-owned isolated physical server lab or faithful emulator with synthetic workloads and no production reachability, diagnose, contain, recover and remove an unfamiliar bare-metal lifecycle incident. The reviewer secretly injects one identity or ownership defect, one BMC/power/firmware defect, one boot/provisioning defect, one inventory/storage/network/first-boot defect, one hardware-health or capacity defect and one maintenance/sanitization/cleanup defect. Work without model-answer material.
deliverables: Named user or fleet operation, request ID, exact physical target, owner, SLO and refusal conditions
Asset, chassis, system, manager, rack, power-feed, switch-edge, storage and controller identity graph
Exact controller, BMC, firmware, UEFI, agent, image, driver and operating-system release contract
BMC TLS, authorization, session, task, event, power and firmware evidence timeline
DHCP, architecture, PXE/iPXE, artifact digest, kernel argument, boot ID and agent callback path
Out-of-band and in-band inspection reconciliation for CPU, memory, storage, NIC, PCI and firmware
Desired/current RAID, physical media, persistent root-device, image-write and boot-artifact evidence
Metadata, instance ID, cloud-init, installed OS, host network, workload readiness and user transaction
RAS, thermal, fan, power, PCIe, media, rack/facility and capacity evidence with policy decisions
Bounded containment, drain, fencing, canary, stop gates and rollback, rebuild or replacement plan
Risk-based serial-bound sanitization verification, validation and disposition evidence
Exact credential, allocation, boot artifact, network, inventory, workload and temporary-state cleanup
evidenceRequirements: Use only reviewer-owned isolated physical hardware or a faithful emulator with synthetic data and workloads
Use no production host, shared management plane, public target, external cloud, customer data or uncontrolled power or load
Reviewer owns credentials, hidden defects, stop authority, scoring and cleanup confirmation
Bind immutable physical identity and current ownership before any action
Keep desired state, accepted task, terminal task, observed hardware, agent, installed OS and user outcome separate
Bind every boot and image artifact to architecture, immutable digest, approved source and request
Use serial or WWN and controller/slot evidence for storage; kernel names or models alone are insufficient
Reconcile out-of-band and in-band inventory with freshness and explicit disagreements
Label corrected, uncorrected, fatal, sensor and media evidence with rates, time, owner and proof limits
Give every mutation an owner, blast radius, stop condition, rollback or rebuild boundary and before/after proof
Choose sanitization from data class, media type, capability and disposition; include verification and reviewer validation
Prove the original user result and exact removal or intentional reconciliation of every created artifact

Explains trust authorization tasks observed state inventory and partial progress

Reconciles inspection RAID persistent disks switch edge and target selection
Proves image write boot artifacts metadata OS network workload and transaction
Interprets RAS sensors media facility trends and survivor reserve
Maintains isolation least privilege evidence preservation and stop gates
Uses drain fence owner-scoped correction canary and rollback rebuild or replacement
Proves method fit verification validation disposition and exact reconciliation
Produces causal timeline bounded claims durable controls owners and retest
